title: Don't Starve
notes: The five-day continuous-survival target is retained under the continuous-game rule. Rubric v5 refines it into ten half-day thresholds of 10 points, using preserved native age and whole-cycle advance within a single episode. Survival is direct progress toward the declared target; optional crafting earns no points. The fixed undeveloped Wilson Long Day snapshot, default resources, disabled DLC and HUD size 10 retain the documented team latency-based difficulty exception. DeepSeek receives two attempts within 21,600 seconds with bounded summarized memory after its first death; Jev receives one attempt within 7,200 seconds. Both new cohorts use controls-v5 and three-second frozen steps where applicable. Historical rubrics, specifications, runtime attribution and evidence remain unchanged; eligible completed DeepSeek evidence is rescored on its first two attempts only.
introduction: Don't Starve is a real-time survival and crafting game with continuous survival rather than a finite ending in this setting. A trial starts Wilson in an undeveloped first-day base-game world with DLC disabled and the official Long Day option, retaining a day/dusk/night cycle. The declared target is five complete native days of continuous survival within one episode. The frozen rubric measures progress toward that target; optional crafting earns no points and survival time is never pooled across deaths. The language model has two attempts within at most six hours, with summarized memory from the first attempt; Jev has one attempt within at most two hours and ends at its first native death. This setting does not measure Adventure Mode completion.
controls: W/A/S/D move. Space performs a nearby contextual action. F attacks a nearby target. Left click performs the primary action at the pointer. Right click performs the secondary action at the pointer. Pointer hover reveals native action labels, and dragging moves an object to a selected destination. Escape opens or closes menus, Tab toggles the map, Q/E rotate the camera, and Return confirms menu selections. Scroll changes zoom or scrolls the visible interface. These are ordinary input bindings, not a strategy. Number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate the native action for items in inventory slots 1 through 10. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
